subject: CuraLogic evaluation MAP, closing gates & acceptance tests
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Torres <elena@curalogic.com>, Samir Patel <samir@curalogic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CuraLogic evaluation MAP, closing gates & acceptance tests

Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) tailored to CuraLogic's evaluation goals. High level: we want to make the pilot decisionable within 6 weeks while protecting production risk and validating latency/cost targets.

Key sections in the attachment:
- Goals & success metrics (latency P50/P95, concordance on sample prompts, embedding recall)
- Exit gates (hard blockers that stop progress) and pass/fail rules for each gate
- Acceptance test suite (smoke tests + 3 representative workflows)
- Responsibilities & owners (R: you / A: Redwood SEs / I: procurement/legal)

Quick summary of proposed acceptance criteria you asked about on the call:
- Performance: P95 < 850ms on canonical prompts at 8k context, 95% of requests during load window
- Quality: 90%+ intent-classification concordance on evaluation set (n=200) with manual spot checks
- Stability: KV cache hit rate > 30% for repeat prefixes during simulated traffic

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) You review the MAP attachment and highlight any redlines (by Tue 02/10)
2) Redwood runs the smoke acceptance tests in our sandbox and shares a log (by Fri 02/13)
3) Joint decision call to sign off on go/no-go for pilot (week of 02/16)

Attachments: CuraLogic_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), acceptance_smoke_tests.md (test spec)

If this timeline looks tight for your procurement/legal teams, flag it and we can extend the decision date without changing test rigor.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Elena Torres <elena@curalogic.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@curalogic.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CuraLogic evaluation MAP, closing gates & acceptance tests

Thanks, Markus. Helpful draft — quick clarifying points from our side:

1) The P95 latency target: is that measured from our integration endpoint to model token completion, or from token emission at the GPU? We need the former for SLA planning.
2) For the quality concordance test: can we include custom prompts that surface our regulatory language (HIPAA-related redactions)? We need at least 50 of the 200 items to be redaction-sensitive.
3) Procurement: our legal team wants to see a proposed data retention window and logs access policy before we commit to the pilot. Can you point us to the sample doc?

Also — can you confirm whether the smoke tests will run in a CuraLogic-dedicated sandbox or Redwood shared sandbox? We prefer isolated runs for the first acceptance pass.

Best,
Elena
Director of Product | CuraLogic

-----
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Torres <elena@curalogic.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CuraLogic evaluation MAP, closing gates & acceptance tests

Elena — quick answers inline and a small update to the MAP planned: 

1) Latency measurement: we will report end-to-end latency from your integration endpoint (round-trip) — that will be the number used for the acceptance gate. We'll include the breakdown (network + processing) in the test logs.

2) Quality set: absolutely — we've left the 200-item set extensible. Please add the 50 redaction-sensitive prompts as a CSV and drop them into the Drive link; we'll fold them into the concordance run.

3) Data retention & logs: Naomi (cc'ed) will share a short policy excerpt. For the pilot we can offer a 30-day logs retention with audit access to your security team.

4) Sandbox: we can provide a dedicated sandbox environment (isolated GPU pool) for your acceptance run. That will mirror the Dedicated offering's networking and privacy controls but on a temporary reservation.

Small MAP update: schedule sweetspot moved one business day to give us time to provision the dedicated sandbox. New proposed milestone for Redwood smoke run: Fri 02/14.

Action items:
- Elena: upload redaction prompt CSV (by Mon 02/09)
- Naomi: attach retention excerpt and confirm access list (by Mon 02/09)
- Redwood SEs (Marissa + infra): provision sandbox and confirm endpoint (ETA Wed 02/11)

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Torres <elena@curalogic.com>, Samir Patel <samir@curalogic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CuraLogic evaluation MAP, closing gates & acceptance tests

Elena / Samir —

Appreciate the quick responses and the scope clarifications. We're aligned on the measurement approach and will proceed with the dedicated sandbox. To restate the updated timeline: 

- Mon 02/09: CuraLogic uploads redaction CSV (noted as received on 02/09) and Naomi shares retention excerpt.
- Wed 02/11: Redwood confirms sandbox endpoint and provisioning complete.
- Fri 02/14: Redwood runs smoke acceptance tests in dedicated sandbox and posts logs to the Drive link.
- Week of 02/16: Joint sign-off call to confirm pilot go/no-go.

Acceptance pass rules (short):
- All hard blockers must be zero incidents: failures to meet P95 latency, data exfiltration signals, or failing redaction sensitivity on >10% of redaction-sensitive prompts.
- Quality: overall concordance >= 90% on the 200-item set (including the 50 redaction items).
- Stability: no >1% error rate during the smoke load window.

If you agree, we'll treat receipt of your uploaded CSV and Naomi's retention excerpt as official inputs and proceed to provision. Once the smoke logs are posted, we'll schedule the sign-off call (I'll send a calendar invite).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above: CuraLogic_MAP_v1.xlsx, acceptance_smoke_tests.md
Drive: https://drive.google.com/curalogic/MAP_v1
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/deal/3491
